name: Ocean Pond Campground (Osceola National Forest)
coordinateNote: Entrance, parking or campsite coordinates from the November 12, 2026 research.
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Sixty-seven lakeside sites: 20 primitive, 28 with water and 19 with electric and water on paved spurs, plus a campers-only beach. It is one of the two kinds of place where camping stays legal in Osceola during general gun season.
access: First come, first served. Stay limit: 14 days per month (National Forests in Florida) Forest Service: 'General gun season runs from mid-November to early January' and all camping is then restricted to designated hunt camps and Ocean Pond Campground. Derived from rule text (opens 7 days after the first day of Zone C antlered deer season, closes 57 days later) and FWC's 2026-27 Zone C start of Nov 7: about Nov 14, 2026 - Jan 10, 2027; the 2026-27 brochure itself was not retrieved. Roadside dispersed camping in Osceola NF is therefore not legal on Nov 21 - Dec 8. Forest Service urges hikers to wear bright colors. Ocean Pond is named as an allowed campground during general gun season.

conditions.summary: Forest Service page shows 'Site Open'. Fees: $12 primitive, $20 water hook-up, $30 electric and water. Whether sites are first-come or bookable is not stated on the page; shower fee for non-campers is listed inconsistently ($5 or $2). (source dated 2026-04-23)

camp.sedanNote: Forest Service: water/electric spurs are paved with 50-foot capacity; the approach road and the $12 primitive sites' surface are not stated.
